fields.why: Methods state 'Nonoverlapping 95% CIs were considered to represent statistically significant differences', and the headline claim ('coverage varied by ... region, social vulnerability index level, and facility size') plus the highest/lowest contrasts can rest only on that rule; every contrast claimed has non-overlapping CIs in the table, so a CI overlap assertion (test) is preferred. A's regression-only reading is defensible under v5 rule (b) because no result sentence invokes the intervals or significance.
Follows procedure_classes: a CI overlap assertion is class test under v5. False is defensible if the stated rule is treated as unused.

Poisson-model CIs are reported for all estimates; with the overlap assertion counted as a test (ci_overlap true) inference is 'CIs and tests'. 'CIs' is defensible under the strict reading that no claim explicitly rests on interval comparison.

brief_issues: CI overlap: v5 says a stated overlap rule counts only when a claim 'actually rests' on it, but does not say whether unqualified difference claims (varied, highest, lowest) in a report whose only stated significance criterion is CI overlap rest on it. Proposed rule: yes, when the article draws difference claims between estimates the rule covers and gives no other test.
